questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with a suitable article: "___ Ganga is a sacred river for millions of people."
questions.explanation: Names of rivers take the definite article: the Ganga, the Cauvery, the Nile.
questions.trick: Rivers, seas, oceans, mountain ranges and groups of islands take 'the'.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct article: "Mount Everest is ___ highest peak in the world."
questions.explanation: A superlative adjective (highest) is preceded by 'the'.
questions.trick: Superlative degree → always 'the'.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option: "The children go to ___ bed at nine o'clock every night."
questions.explanation: 'Go to bed' means going to sleep — bed is used for its primary purpose, so no article is used.
questions.trick: bed, school, church, hospital, prison, college take no article when used for their main purpose.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "My sister plays ___ violin beautifully."
questions.explanation: In British usage, musical instruments take 'the' after 'play': play the violin, play the veena.
questions.trick: Play + instrument → 'the'; play + game → no article.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "The boys play ___ cricket every evening."
questions.explanation: Names of games and sports do not take an article: play cricket, play football.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct article: "Kalidasa is often called ___ Shakespeare of India."
questions.explanation: When a proper noun is used to mean 'one like', in a unique comparison (the Shakespeare of India), 'the' is used.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "___ sun sets in the west."
questions.explanation: Things that are one of a kind (the sun, the moon, the sky) take 'the'.
questions.trick: Unique objects → 'the'.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct article: "He is ___ one-eyed man."
questions.explanation: 'One' begins with a 'w' (consonant) sound, so 'a one-eyed man' is correct.
questions.trick: Articles follow the SOUND, not the spelling: 'an' before a vowel sound, 'a' before a consonant sound.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "There is ___ university in almost every district of Tamil Nadu."
questions.explanation: 'University' begins with a 'yu' (consonant) sound, so 'a' is used.
questions.trick: Articles follow the SOUND, not the spelling: 'an' before a vowel sound, 'a' before a consonant sound.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "Half ___ hour is enough to finish this task."
questions.explanation: The 'h' in 'hour' is silent, so it begins with a vowel sound: half an hour.
questions.trick: Articles follow the SOUND, not the spelling: 'an' before a vowel sound, 'a' before a consonant sound.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "Our reading club meets once ___ week."
questions.explanation: Expressions of frequency use 'a/an': once a week, twice a day.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct article: "What ___ honour it is to meet you, sir!"
questions.explanation: 'Honour' starts with a silent 'h', so it takes 'an'; exclamations with 'What' use a/an before a singular countable noun.
questions.trick: Articles follow the SOUND, not the spelling: 'an' before a vowel sound, 'a' before a consonant sound.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "He is such ___ fool that everyone laughs at him."
questions.explanation: 'Such' is followed by 'a/an' before a singular countable noun: such a fool.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "There is ___ owl sitting on the banyan tree."
questions.explanation: 'Owl' begins with a vowel sound, and 'There is' introduces something new, so 'an' is correct.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "The bus was moving at sixty kilometres ___ hour."
questions.explanation: Rate expressions use a/an (sixty kilometres an hour); 'hour' has a silent h, so 'an'.
questions.trick: Articles follow the SOUND, not the spelling: 'an' before a vowel sound, 'a' before a consonant sound.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct article: "___ Hindu is an English newspaper published from Chennai."
questions.explanation: Names of newspapers take 'the': The Hindu, The Times of India.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "___ Himalayas protect India from the cold winds of Central Asia."
questions.explanation: Mountain ranges take 'the' (the Himalayas, the Western Ghats), unlike single peaks.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option: "___ gold is a precious metal."
questions.explanation: Material nouns used in a general sense take no article: Gold is a precious metal.
questions.trick: Material/abstract nouns in a general sense → no article.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "___ rich should help the poor."
questions.explanation: 'The + adjective' stands for a whole class of people: the rich, the poor, the blind.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct article: "Who is ___ best student in your class?"
questions.explanation: A superlative (best) takes 'the'.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "Her brother is ___ M.A. in History."
questions.explanation: The letter M is pronounced 'em', which begins with a vowel sound, so 'an M.A.'.
questions.trick: Articles follow the SOUND, not the spelling: 'an' before a vowel sound, 'a' before a consonant sound.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "There was ___ European tourist on our bus."
questions.explanation: 'European' begins with a 'yu' sound (consonant), so 'a European'.
questions.trick: Articles follow the SOUND, not the spelling: 'an' before a vowel sound, 'a' before a consonant sound.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option: "The Taj Mahal was built by ___ Shah Jahan."
questions.explanation: Names of persons do not take an article.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blanks: "___ more you read, ___ more you learn."
questions.explanation: In parallel comparatives ('the more …, the more …') 'the' is used before both comparatives.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct verb: "The Prime Minister, along with his ministers, ___ expected tomorrow."
questions.explanation: The subject is 'The Prime Minister' (singular); 'along with his ministers' does not change it.
questions.trick: With / along with / as well as / together with do not change the subject — the verb agrees with the FIRST subject.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct verb: "Bread and butter ___ my usual breakfast."
questions.explanation: Two nouns that together express one idea or one dish take a singular verb.
questions.trick: Two nouns = one idea (bread and butter, rice and curry) → singular verb.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "Not only the teacher but also the students ___ invited to the function."
questions.explanation: With 'not only … but also', the verb agrees with the nearer subject, 'the students' (plural).
questions.trick: Either/or, neither/nor, not only/but also → verb agrees with the nearer subject.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct verb: "Neither of the two answers ___ correct."
questions.explanation: 'Neither of' takes a singular verb in standard usage: Neither of them is …

questions.prompt: Choose the correct verb: "The number of students in this school ___ increasing every year."
questions.explanation: 'The number of' is singular (the subject is 'number').
questions.trick: THE number → singular; A number → plural.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "The police ___ arrested the thief."
questions.explanation: 'Police' is always plural in form and use, so it takes a plural verb.
questions.trick: Police, cattle, people, poultry → always plural.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "The cattle ___ grazing in the field."
questions.explanation: 'Cattle' is a plural noun and takes a plural verb.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct verb: "These scissors ___ very sharp."
questions.explanation: Nouns naming things made of two parts (scissors, trousers, spectacles) take a plural verb.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct verb: "The news ___ not true."
questions.explanation: 'News' looks plural but is singular, so it takes 'is'.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "Many a student ___ failed in the test."
questions.explanation: 'Many a' is followed by a singular noun and a singular verb.
questions.trick: 'Many a' + singular noun + singular verb.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct verb: "One of my friends ___ a doctor."
questions.explanation: The subject is 'One' (singular), not 'friends'.
questions.trick: 'One of' + plural noun + SINGULAR verb.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct verb: "Five kilometres ___ a long distance to walk."
questions.explanation: A distance taken as one total amount takes a singular verb.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct verb: "The committee ___ divided in their opinions."
questions.explanation: When members of a collective noun act as individuals (divided in THEIR opinions), the verb is plural.
questions.trick: Collective noun as one unit → singular; members acting separately → plural.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "The jury ___ given its verdict."
questions.explanation: The jury acts as a single body here ('its verdict'), so the verb is singular.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "Everybody in the hall ___ standing when the chief guest arrived."
questions.explanation: 'Everybody' is singular, and the past time (arrived) needs 'was'.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct verb: "The furniture in these rooms ___ new."
questions.explanation: 'Furniture' is an uncountable noun and takes a singular verb.
questions.trick: Furniture, luggage, information, advice, scenery → uncountable, singular.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "The poor ___ often denied good medical care."
questions.explanation: 'The poor' means poor people — a plural class — so it takes a plural verb.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct verb: "'Gulliver's Travels' ___ written by Jonathan Swift."
questions.explanation: The title of a single book is singular even if it looks plural.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "Two-thirds of the work ___ been completed."
questions.explanation: With fractions, the verb agrees with the noun after 'of'; 'work' is uncountable, so singular.
questions.trick: Fraction/percentage + of + noun → verb agrees with that noun.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct verb: "He is one of those men who ___ always late."
questions.explanation: The relative pronoun 'who' refers to 'men' (plural), so the verb in the clause is plural.

questions.prompt: Select the grammatically correct sentence.
options: The quality of the mangoes are good.
The quality of the mangoes were good.
The quality of the mangoes have been good.
The quality of the mangoes is good.
questions.explanation: The subject is 'quality' (singular); 'of the mangoes' only describes it.
questions.trick: Ignore the 'of …' phrase and find the true subject.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct question tag: "She can swim well, ___?"
questions.explanation: The statement is positive with 'can', so the tag is 'can't she?'.
questions.trick: Positive statement → negative tag; negative statement → positive tag; reuse the helping verb and a pronoun.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct question tag: "You are coming with us, ___?"
questions.explanation: Positive statement with 'are' → negative tag 'aren't you?'.
questions.trick: Positive statement → negative tag; negative statement → positive tag; reuse the helping verb and a pronoun.

questions.prompt: Select the correct question tag: "I am your friend, ___?"
questions.explanation: The accepted negative tag for 'I am' is 'aren't I?' ('am I not?' in formal style).
questions.trick: I am … → aren't I?

questions.prompt: Choose the correct question tag: "Nobody called me while I was out, ___?"
questions.explanation: 'Nobody' makes the statement negative, so the tag is positive; indefinite pronouns like nobody/everyone take 'they' in the tag.
questions.trick: Nobody/no one/nothing are negative → positive tag.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct question tag: "Close the door, ___?"
questions.explanation: An imperative (request/command) takes 'will you?' as its tag.
questions.trick: Imperative → will you?; Let's → shall we?

questions.prompt: Select the suitable tag: "Let's play chess after dinner, ___?"
questions.explanation: A suggestion beginning with 'Let's' always takes the tag 'shall we?'.
questions.trick: Let's … → shall we?

questions.prompt: Choose the correct question tag: "There is a temple near the river, ___?"
questions.explanation: When the sentence begins with 'There is', the tag repeats 'there': isn't there?

questions.prompt: Choose the correct question tag: "He hardly works these days, ___?"
questions.explanation: 'Hardly' gives the sentence a negative meaning, so the tag is positive: does he?
questions.trick: hardly, scarcely, seldom, barely, never, few, little → positive tag.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct question tag: "Everyone enjoyed the party, ___?"
questions.explanation: Everyone/everybody take 'they' in the tag; a positive past statement takes 'didn't they?'.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct question tag: "You have finished the work, ___?"
questions.explanation: The helping verb is 'have', so the negative tag is 'haven't you?'.
questions.trick: Positive statement → negative tag; negative statement → positive tag; reuse the helping verb and a pronoun.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct question tag: "Ravi used to live in Madurai, ___?"
questions.explanation: 'Used to' takes 'did' in the tag: didn't he?

questions.prompt: Choose the correct question tag: "This is your pen, ___?"
questions.explanation: 'This' and 'that' become 'it' in the tag.
questions.trick: this/that → it; these/those → they.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct question tag: "She never tells lies, ___?"
questions.explanation: 'Never' makes the statement negative, so the tag is positive: does she?

questions.prompt: Choose the correct question tag: "Raja will come tomorrow, ___?"
questions.explanation: Positive statement with 'will' → 'won't he?'.
questions.trick: Positive statement → negative tag; negative statement → positive tag; reuse the helping verb and a pronoun.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct question tag: "We must leave now, ___?"
questions.explanation: The tag repeats the modal 'must' in the negative: mustn't we?

questions.prompt: Choose the correct question tag: "Few people knew the answer, ___?"
questions.explanation: 'Few' has a negative sense (almost none), so the tag is positive: did they?

questions.prompt: Choose the correct question tag: "The children were playing in the park, ___?"
questions.explanation: Positive statement with 'were' → negative tag 'weren't they?'.

questions.prompt: In "She sings sweetly," the word 'sweetly' is a/an:
questions.explanation: 'Sweetly' tells how she sings — it modifies the verb, so it is an adverb.

questions.prompt: In "The athlete ran fast to catch the bus," the word 'fast' is a/an:
questions.explanation: Here 'fast' modifies the verb 'ran' (how he ran), so it is an adverb.
questions.trick: A word's part of speech depends on its JOB in the sentence, not on the word itself.

questions.prompt: In "My uncle drives a fast car," the word 'fast' is a/an:
questions.explanation: Here 'fast' describes the noun 'car', so it is an adjective.
questions.trick: A word's part of speech depends on its JOB in the sentence, not on the word itself.

questions.prompt: In "Alas! The old poet is no more," the word 'Alas' is a/an:
questions.explanation: 'Alas' expresses sudden sorrow and stands apart from the sentence, so it is an interjection.

questions.prompt: In "The dictionary is on the shelf," the word 'on' is a/an:
questions.explanation: 'On' shows the relation between 'dictionary' and 'shelf', so it is a preposition.

questions.prompt: In "The guests arrived after we had finished dinner," the word 'after' is a/an:
questions.explanation: 'After' joins a full clause (we had finished dinner) to the main clause, so it works as a conjunction.
questions.trick: after/before/since + clause (subject + verb) → conjunction; + noun only → preposition.

questions.prompt: In "She took a short nap after lunch," the word 'after' is a/an:
questions.explanation: 'After' is followed by the noun 'lunch' (its object), so it is a preposition.

questions.prompt: In "Honesty is the best policy," the word 'Honesty' is a/an:
questions.explanation: 'Honesty' names a quality — it is an abstract noun.

questions.prompt: In "Each boy received a prize," the word 'Each' is a/an:
questions.explanation: 'Each' qualifies the noun 'boy' that follows it, so in school grammar it is a distributive adjective. (In 'Each of them received a prize' it would be a pronoun.)
questions.trick: Followed by a noun → adjective; standing alone in place of a noun → pronoun.

questions.prompt: In "This is my grandfather's house," the word 'This' is a/an:
questions.explanation: 'This' stands alone in place of a noun (it is the subject), so it is a demonstrative pronoun.
questions.trick: A word's part of speech depends on its JOB in the sentence, not on the word itself.

questions.prompt: In "The farmers work hard in the fields," the word 'hard' is a/an:
questions.explanation: 'Hard' tells how they work, modifying the verb 'work', so it is an adverb.

questions.prompt: In "Kumar is taller than his brother," the word 'than' is a/an:
questions.explanation: In school (Wren & Martin) grammar, 'than' after a comparative is treated as a conjunction (… than his brother is).

questions.prompt: In "I have never seen a tiger in the wild," the word 'never' is a/an:
questions.explanation: 'Never' is an adverb of frequency/time modifying 'have seen'.

questions.prompt: In "She herself cooked the whole meal," the word 'herself' is a/an:
questions.explanation: 'Herself' is an emphatic (reflexive-form) pronoun that stresses the subject 'She'.

questions.prompt: In "He is the doctor whom everyone trusts," the word 'whom' is a/an:
questions.explanation: 'Whom' is a relative pronoun: it refers back to 'the doctor' and is the object of 'trusts'.

questions.prompt: In "The lift went down slowly," the word 'down' is a/an:
questions.explanation: 'Down' has no object after it and tells the direction of 'went', so it is an adverb.
questions.trick: Preposition needs an object (down the hill); with no object it is an adverb (went down).

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a collective noun?
questions.explanation: 'Herd' names a group of animals taken as one whole, so it is a collective noun.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is an abstract noun?
questions.explanation: 'Childhood' names a state or period that cannot be touched; 'childish' is an adjective.
questions.trick: Suffixes -hood, -ness, -ship, -dom, -ity often make abstract nouns.

questions.prompt: The word 'beautify' is a/an:
questions.explanation: 'Beautify' means 'to make beautiful' — an action word, so it is a verb.
questions.trick: Suffixes -ify, -ise/-ize, -en often form verbs.

questions.prompt: Identify the adverb in the sentence: "The old man walked slowly to the temple."
questions.explanation: 'Slowly' describes how the man walked, so it is the adverb.

questions.prompt: Identify the conjunction in the sentence: "I waited for an hour, but he did not come."
questions.explanation: 'But' joins the two clauses and shows contrast.

questions.prompt: Choose the noun form of 'brave'.
questions.explanation: 'Bravery' is the noun; 'bravely' is an adverb and 'braver/bravest' are comparative forms.

questions.prompt: Choose the adjective form of 'danger'.
questions.explanation: 'Dangerous' describes a noun (a dangerous road), so it is the adjective form.

questions.prompt: Choose the verb form of 'strong'.
questions.explanation: 'Strengthen' means 'to make strong' (verb); 'strength' is the noun.

questions.prompt: Choose the noun form of the verb 'decide'.
questions.explanation: 'Decision' is the noun; 'decisive' is an adjective and 'decisively' an adverb.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the correct preposition: "Jawaharlal Nehru was born ___ 14 November 1889."
questions.explanation: A specific date takes 'on'.
questions.trick: AT a clock time, ON a day/date, IN a month/year/season.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct preposition: "The express train arrives ___ 6.30 p.m."
questions.explanation: A precise clock time takes 'at'.
questions.trick: AT a clock time, ON a day/date, IN a month/year/season.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "My sister is very fond ___ classical music."
questions.explanation: The fixed expression is 'fond of'.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "Meena is good ___ mathematics."
questions.explanation: We say 'good at' a subject or skill.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "The heavy rain prevented us ___ going out."
questions.explanation: 'Prevent someone from doing something' is the correct pattern.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct preposition: "The boy jumped ___ the pond to save the puppy."
questions.explanation: 'Into' shows movement from outside to inside; 'in' shows position.
questions.trick: Movement inside → into; position inside → in.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "He has been ill ___ last Monday."
questions.explanation: 'Since' is used with a point of time (last Monday) in perfect tenses.
questions.trick: SINCE + point of time; FOR + length of time.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "My grandparents have lived in this village ___ forty years."
questions.explanation: 'For' is used with a period of time (forty years).
questions.trick: SINCE + point of time; FOR + length of time.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "Divide the sweets equally ___ the two children."
questions.explanation: 'Between' is used for two persons or things.
questions.trick: Between → two; among → more than two.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "The teacher distributed the notebooks ___ the forty students."
questions.explanation: 'Among' is used for more than two.
questions.trick: Between → two; among → more than two.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "He insisted ___ paying the bill himself."
questions.explanation: The verb 'insist' is followed by 'on'.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "I congratulate you ___ your brilliant success."
questions.explanation: 'Congratulate somebody on something' is the standard usage.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "Father was angry ___ my younger brother for breaking the vase."
questions.explanation: In standard usage we are 'angry with' a person and 'angry at' a thing or situation.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "Ramesh is senior ___ me by two years."
questions.explanation: Latin comparatives (senior, junior, superior, inferior, prior) take 'to', not 'than'.
questions.trick: senior/junior/superior/inferior/prior → TO, never 'than'.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "Please write the answers ___ ink."
questions.explanation: We write 'in ink' (the medium) but 'with a pen' (the instrument).

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "The clerk was accused ___ theft."
questions.explanation: 'Accused of' is the fixed pattern (but 'charged with').

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "The child is suffering ___ high fever."
questions.explanation: 'Suffer from' an illness is the correct usage.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "Every citizen should abide ___ the law."
questions.explanation: The phrasal verb is 'abide by' (obey).

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "I will wait for you ___ the bus stop."
questions.explanation: 'At' is used for a particular point or place where something happens.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "We travelled ___ Chennai to Madurai by train."
questions.explanation: The pair 'from … to …' marks a starting point and destination.

questions.prompt: Spot the part of the sentence that has an error: "She gave me / many informations / about the / new course."
questions.explanation: 'Information' is uncountable — it has no plural and cannot take 'many'. Correct: 'much information'.
questions.trick: Uncountable: information, advice, furniture, luggage, equipment — no plural form.

questions.prompt: Spot the part of the sentence that has an error: "He did not / went to school / because he / was ill."
questions.explanation: After 'did not' the base form is used: 'did not go'.
questions.trick: do/does/did + base form of the verb.

questions.prompt: Spot the part of the sentence that has an error: "I am knowing / him / ever since / my childhood."
questions.explanation: 'Know' is a stative verb and is not used in continuous tenses; with 'since' the present perfect is needed: 'I have known him'.
questions.trick: Stative verbs (know, believe, love, own, understand) are not used in -ing tenses.

questions.prompt: Spot the part of the sentence that has an error: "She returned back / from Delhi / late last / evening."
questions.explanation: 'Returned back' is redundant — 'return' already means 'come back'.
questions.trick: Avoid redundancy: return back, repeat again, revert back.

questions.prompt: Spot the part of the sentence that has an error: "Neither the captain / nor his players / was present / at the meeting."
questions.explanation: With neither … nor, the verb agrees with the nearer subject 'his players' (plural): 'were present'.

questions.prompt: Spot the part of the sentence that has an error: "My father has been working / in this office / since five years / and is happy here."
questions.explanation: 'Five years' is a period of time, so 'for' is needed, not 'since'.
questions.trick: SINCE + point of time; FOR + length of time.

questions.prompt: Punctuate correctly: ramu the captain of our team scored a century
options: Ramu the captain of our team, scored a century.
Ramu, the captain of our team, scored a century.
Ramu, the captain of our team scored a century.
Ramu the captain, of our team scored a century.
questions.explanation: A phrase in apposition (the captain of our team) is enclosed between two commas.
questions.trick: Extra information in the middle of a sentence → a pair of commas.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "The dog wagged ___ tail happily."
questions.explanation: 'Its' (no apostrophe) is the possessive; 'it's' means 'it is' or 'it has'.
questions.trick: it's = it is / it has; its = belonging to it.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct possessive form for 'the toys belonging to the children'.
questions.explanation: 'Children' is a plural that does not end in 's', so we add 's: children's.
questions.trick: Plural ending in -s → add only ' (girls'); plural without -s → add 's (men's, children's).

questions.prompt: Which punctuation mark should end the sentence "How brave the little girl was"?
questions.explanation: A sentence beginning with 'How/What' that expresses strong feeling is exclamatory and ends with '!'.

questions.prompt: Choose the punctuation mark that fits the blank: "The basket contained three fruits ___ mangoes, bananas and grapes."
questions.explanation: A colon is used to introduce a list after a complete clause.

questions.prompt: In the word "don't", the apostrophe stands for:
questions.explanation: In contractions the apostrophe marks the missing letter(s): do not → don't.

questions.prompt: Which phrase is correctly hyphenated?
questions.explanation: A compound adjective before a noun is hyphenated (well-known), but the noun itself is not joined to it.

questions.prompt: In a formal letter, the salutation 'Dear Sir' is usually followed by a:
questions.explanation: In Indian and British letter-writing, the salutation (Dear Sir,) and the subscription (Yours faithfully,) are followed by a comma.

questions.prompt: Which is the correct way to punctuate this reported question: she asked me where I lived
options: She asked me where I lived?
She asked me where did I live?
She asked me where I lived.
questions.explanation: An indirect (reported) question ends with a full stop, not a question mark.
questions.trick: Reported question → full stop, statement word order.

questions.prompt: Punctuate correctly: however the plan failed
questions.explanation: An introductory word like 'However' is followed by a comma.

questions.prompt: Punctuate correctly: i am tired said meena
questions.explanation: When the reporting clause follows the quotation, the quoted statement ends with a comma inside the closing quotation marks.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses the semicolon correctly?
options: The rain stopped; and the children went out to play.
The rain; stopped the children went out to play.
The rain stopped; the children went out to play.
The rain stopped, the children; went out to play.
questions.explanation: A semicolon joins two closely related independent clauses without a conjunction.
questions.trick: Semicolon replaces 'and/but' between two full clauses — never use both together.

questions.prompt: Punctuate correctly: yes i will attend the meeting
options: Yes I will, attend the meeting.
Yes, I will attend the meeting.
Yes. I will attend, the meeting.
Yes I, will attend the meeting.
questions.explanation: 'Yes' and 'No' at the beginning of a reply are followed by a comma.

questions.prompt: Punctuate correctly: ravi come here at once
questions.explanation: The name of the person addressed (vocative) is separated by a comma.

questions.prompt: Punctuate correctly: what a lovely garden this is
options: What a lovely garden this is!
What a lovely garden this is?
what a lovely garden this is.
What a lovely garden, this is.
questions.explanation: An exclamatory sentence begins with a capital letter and ends with an exclamation mark.

questions.prompt: Punctuate correctly: where do you live asked the stranger
options: "Where do you live?" asked the stranger.
"Where do you live," asked the stranger?
Where do you live? "asked the stranger."
"Where do you live" asked the stranger?
questions.explanation: The question mark belongs to the spoken question and goes inside the quotation marks; the sentence ends with a full stop.

questions.prompt: The room used by all the teachers is called the ___ room.
questions.explanation: For a plural noun ending in -s, only an apostrophe is added: teachers'.

questions.prompt: Which use of the apostrophe is correct on a shop board?
questions.explanation: Ordinary plurals do not take an apostrophe; the apostrophe is for possession or omission.

questions.prompt: Punctuate correctly: hurrah we have won the match
options: Hurrah. we have won the match!

questions.explanation: Brackets set off additional information that the sentence could do without, e.g. 'Chennai (formerly Madras)'.

questions.prompt: Punctuate correctly the reported statement: he said that he was busy

He said that he was busy.
questions.explanation: Indirect speech uses no quotation marks and no comma before 'that'.

questions.prompt: Change into passive voice: "The cat killed the rat."
options: The rat is killed by the cat.
The rat has been killed by the cat.
The rat was killed by the cat.
The rat had been killed by the cat.
questions.explanation: Simple past active (killed) → was/were + past participle.
questions.trick: Active → passive: object becomes subject, verb becomes the right form of 'be' + past participle, subject goes after 'by'. Keep the tense.

questions.prompt: Change into passive voice: "Ravi is painting the wall."
options: The wall is painted by Ravi.
The wall is being painted by Ravi.
The wall was being painted by Ravi.
The wall has been painted by Ravi.
questions.explanation: Present continuous active → is/am/are + being + past participle.
questions.trick: Continuous tenses add 'being' in the passive.

questions.prompt: Change into passive voice: "They have built a new bridge across the river."
options: A new bridge was built across the river by them.
A new bridge has been built across the river by them.
A new bridge is being built across the river by them.
A new bridge had built across the river by them.
questions.explanation: Present perfect active → has/have + been + past participle.
questions.trick: Perfect tenses add 'been' in the passive.

questions.prompt: Change into passive voice: "The police had caught the thief before sunset."
options: The thief was caught by the police before sunset.
The thief has been caught by the police before sunset.
The thief had caught by the police before sunset.
The thief had been caught by the police before sunset.
questions.explanation: Past perfect active → had + been + past participle.
questions.trick: Active → passive: object becomes subject, verb becomes the right form of 'be' + past participle, subject goes after 'by'. Keep the tense.

questions.prompt: Change into passive voice: "She will sing a devotional song."
options: A devotional song will be sang by her.
A devotional song will sung by her.
A devotional song will be sung by her.
A devotional song would be sung by her.
questions.explanation: Simple future active → will/shall + be + past participle (sung, not sang).
questions.trick: Active → passive: object becomes subject, verb becomes the right form of 'be' + past participle, subject goes after 'by'. Keep the tense.

questions.prompt: Change into passive voice: "Open the window."
options: The window be opened by you.
questions.explanation: An imperative command becomes passive with 'Let + object + be + past participle'.
questions.trick: Imperative → passive: Let + object + be + past participle.

questions.prompt: Change into passive voice: "Please help me."
options: I am requested to be helped.
You are requested to help me.
Help is being requested by me.
questions.explanation: A polite request with 'please/kindly' is made passive as 'You are requested to …'.
questions.trick: please/kindly + imperative → You are requested to …

questions.prompt: Change into passive voice: "Who taught you English?"
options: By whom you were taught English?
By whom were you taught English?
Who was taught English by you?
Whom were you taught English by them?
questions.explanation: 'Who' becomes 'By whom' in the passive, and question word order (were you) is kept.
questions.trick: Who → By whom; Whom → Who … by?

questions.prompt: Change into passive voice: "Did he write this letter?"
options: Was this letter written by him?
Is this letter written by him?
Did this letter written by him?
Was this letter wrote by him?
questions.explanation: A simple past question with 'did' becomes 'Was/Were + subject + past participle?'.

questions.prompt: Change into passive voice: "Do not touch the live wires."
options: The live wires are not touched.
Let not the live wires touched.
The live wires do not be touched.
Let the live wires not be touched.
questions.explanation: A negative imperative becomes 'Let + object + not + be + past participle'.
questions.trick: Imperative → passive: Let + object + be + past participle.

questions.prompt: Change into passive voice: "Someone has stolen my bicycle."
questions.explanation: The agent 'someone' is vague and is usually dropped; present perfect → has been + past participle.
questions.trick: Drop vague agents (someone, people, they, nobody) in the passive.

questions.prompt: Change into passive voice: "People speak English all over the world."
options: English is spoken all over the world.
English was spoken all over the world.
English is speaking all over the world.
English has spoken all over the world.
questions.explanation: Simple present active → is/are + past participle; the vague agent 'people' is dropped.

questions.prompt: Change into passive voice: "The headmaster gave Kumar a prize."
options: Kumar is given a prize by the headmaster.
Kumar was gave a prize by the headmaster.
Kumar was given a prize by the headmaster.
A prize was given Kumar by headmaster to.
questions.explanation: With two objects, the indirect object (Kumar) can become the subject; simple past → was + given.
questions.trick: Verbs with two objects (give, show, teach, tell) can have two passive forms.

questions.prompt: Change into active voice: "The match was won by our team."
options: Our team has won the match.
Our team had won the match.
questions.explanation: 'Was won' is simple past passive, so the active is in the simple past: won.

questions.prompt: Change into active voice: "The letters are being typed by the clerk."
options: The clerk was typing the letters.
The clerk has typed the letters.
The clerk is typing the letters.
questions.explanation: 'Are being typed' is present continuous passive → active 'is typing'.

questions.prompt: Change into active voice: "The work will have been completed by them by Friday."
options: They will complete the work by Friday.
They will be completing the work by Friday.
They will have completed the work by Friday.
They would have completed the work by Friday.
questions.explanation: 'Will have been completed' is future perfect passive → active 'will have completed'.

questions.prompt: Change into passive voice: "Her rude behaviour surprised me."
options: I am surprised at her rude behaviour.
I was surprised at her rude behaviour.
I was surprised to her rude behaviour.
Her rude behaviour was surprised by me.
questions.explanation: Some verbs take a preposition other than 'by' in the passive: surprised at, known to, pleased with, filled with.
questions.trick: known TO, surprised AT, pleased WITH, filled WITH, interested IN.

questions.prompt: Change into passive voice: "Everybody knows Mahatma Gandhi."
options: Mahatma Gandhi is known to everybody.
Mahatma Gandhi was known to everybody.
Mahatma Gandhi is knowing to everybody.
Everybody is known to Mahatma Gandhi.
questions.explanation: 'Know' takes 'to' in the passive, and the tense stays simple present: is known.
questions.trick: known TO, surprised AT, pleased WITH, filled WITH.

questions.prompt: Change into passive voice: "The bottle contains milk."
options: Milk was contained in the bottle.
The bottle is contained by milk.
Milk is contained in the bottle.
Milk is containing in the bottle.
questions.explanation: 'Contain' takes 'in' in the passive; simple present → is + past participle.

questions.prompt: Which of these sentences is in the passive voice?
options: Rajaraja Chola built the Brihadeeswarar temple.
The Brihadeeswarar temple was built by Rajaraja Chola.
The Cholas were great temple builders.
The Brihadeeswarar temple stands in Thanjavur.
questions.explanation: A passive sentence has 'be + past participle' and the doer comes after 'by' (or is omitted).

questions.prompt: Which sentence CANNOT be changed into the passive voice?
questions.explanation: 'Slept' is intransitive — it has no object, so it has no passive form.
questions.trick: Only transitive verbs (verbs with an object) have a passive.

questions.prompt: Change into passive voice: "Is she writing a story?"
options: Is a story being written by her?
Is a story written by her?
Was a story being written by her?
Has a story been written by her?
questions.explanation: Present continuous question → Is/Are + object + being + past participle?

questions.prompt: Change into passive voice: "They were watching a film."
options: A film is being watched by them.
A film was watched by them.
A film had been watched by them.
A film was being watched by them.
questions.explanation: Past continuous active → was/were + being + past participle.

questions.prompt: Change into passive voice: "We must obey the traffic rules."
options: The traffic rules must obeyed by us.
The traffic rules must have been obeyed by us.
The traffic rules must be obeyed by us.
The traffic rules must be obey by us.
questions.explanation: Modal + be + past participle: must be obeyed.
questions.trick: Modals (can, must, should, may) → modal + be + past participle.

questions.prompt: Change into passive voice: "One should keep one's promises."
questions.explanation: Modal + be + past participle; the indefinite agent 'one' is dropped.

questions.prompt: Change into passive voice: "Why did you beat the dog?"
options: Why the dog was beaten by you?
Why was the dog beaten by you?
Why was the dog beat by you?
Why did the dog beaten by you?
questions.explanation: A wh-question keeps question order in the passive: Why + was + subject + past participle (beaten).

questions.prompt: Change into passive voice: "The doctor advised him to take rest."
options: He is advised by the doctor to take rest.
He was advised by the doctor to take rest.
He was advise by the doctor to take rest.
To take rest was advised him by the doctor.
questions.explanation: The person advised becomes the subject; simple past → was + advised.

questions.prompt: Change into passive voice: "Let him do this work."
options: Let this work is done by him.
This work be done by him.
Let this work been done by him.
Let this work be done by him.
questions.explanation: 'Let + object + be + past participle + by …' is the passive of a 'Let' sentence.
questions.trick: Imperative → passive: Let + object + be + past participle.

questions.prompt: Change into passive voice: "The farmers grow sugarcane in this area."
options: Sugarcane is grown by the farmers in this area.
Sugarcane was grown by the farmers in this area.
Sugarcane is growing by the farmers in this area.
Sugarcane has grown by the farmers in this area.
questions.explanation: Simple present → is/are + past participle (grown).

questions.prompt: Change into passive voice: "Who broke this glass?"
options: By whom this glass was broken?
By whom was this glass broke?
By whom was this glass broken?
Who was this glass broken by them?
questions.explanation: 'Who' → 'By whom', question order kept, past participle 'broken'.
questions.trick: Who → By whom

questions.prompt: Change into passive voice: "They elected him captain of the team."
options: He is elected captain of the team by them.
Captain of the team was elected him.
He was elected captain of the team.
He was elect captain of the team by them.
questions.explanation: The object 'him' becomes the subject 'He'; simple past → was elected; the complement 'captain' stays after the verb.

questions.prompt: Change into active voice: "The thief was being chased by the villagers."
options: The villagers were chasing the thief.
The villagers are chasing the thief.
The villagers had been chasing the thief.
questions.explanation: 'Was being chased' is past continuous passive → 'were chasing'.

questions.prompt: Change into active voice: "The answer sheets have been corrected by the examiner."
options: The examiner has corrected the answer sheets.
The examiner had corrected the answer sheets.
The examiner corrected the answer sheets.
The examiner is correcting the answer sheets.
questions.explanation: 'Have been corrected' is present perfect passive → 'has corrected' (subject 'examiner' is singular).

questions.prompt: Change into active voice: "The guests will be welcomed by the principal."
options: The principal would welcome the guests.
The principal will be welcoming the guests.
The principal will welcome the guests.
questions.explanation: 'Will be welcomed' is simple future passive → 'will welcome'.

questions.prompt: Select the correct passive form: "We know that the earth is round."
options: It was known that the earth is round.
The earth is knowing to be round.
It is known that the earth is round.
That the earth is round is knowing.
questions.explanation: With 'that'-clauses after verbs like know/believe/say, the impersonal passive 'It is known that …' is used (or 'The earth is known to be round').
questions.trick: Impersonal passive: It is said / believed / known that …

questions.prompt: Change into passive voice: "Somebody should inform the police."
questions.explanation: Modal + be + past participle; the vague agent 'somebody' is dropped.

questions.prompt: Change into passive voice: "The audience praised the singer warmly."
options: The singer was warmly praised by the audience.
The singer is warmly praised by the audience.
The audience was warmly praised by the singer.
The singer was warmly praising by the audience.
questions.explanation: Simple past → was + past participle; the doer (audience) follows 'by'.

questions.prompt: In every passive voice construction, the main verb is in its:
questions.explanation: Passive = form of 'be' + past participle (written, sung, taken).

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the correct tense: "Water ___ at 100 °C at sea level."
questions.explanation: Scientific facts and universal truths are expressed in the simple present.
questions.trick: Universal truth → simple present.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "Look! The baby ___ peacefully."
questions.explanation: 'Look!' shows an action happening at this moment → present continuous.
questions.trick: Look!/Listen!/now/at present → present continuous.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "I ___ my homework already, so I can play now."
questions.explanation: An action just completed with a present result ('so I can play now') takes the present perfect.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "She ___ in Chennai since 2015."
questions.explanation: An action that began in the past and is still continuing (since 2015) takes the present perfect continuous.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "The patient ___ before the doctor came."
questions.explanation: Of two past actions, the earlier one takes the past perfect (had died), the later one the simple past (came).
questions.trick: Earlier of two past actions → had + past participle.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "While I ___ a bath, the phone rang."
questions.explanation: A longer action in progress interrupted by a short one takes the past continuous.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "My uncle ___ to Delhi last week."
questions.explanation: A definite past time (last week) needs the simple past.
questions.trick: yesterday / last … / … ago → simple past, never present perfect.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "I ___ him at the market two days ago."
questions.explanation: 'Two days ago' is a definite past time, so the simple past is used.
questions.trick: yesterday / last … / … ago → simple past, never present perfect.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "By next March, she ___ her course."
questions.explanation: 'By + future time' signals the future perfect.
questions.trick: by + future time → will have + past participle.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "If it rains heavily, we ___ the match."
questions.explanation: First conditional: If + simple present, … will + base verb.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "If I were rich, I ___ a big house for my parents."
questions.explanation: Second conditional (unreal present): If + past (were), … would + base verb.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "If he had taken the medicine, he ___ recovered."
questions.explanation: Third conditional: If + past perfect, … would have + past participle.
questions.trick: If + had + V3 → would have + V3.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "They ___ cricket when it started raining."
questions.explanation: An action in progress in the past when another action happened → past continuous.

questions.prompt: Identify the tense: "She has been teaching for twenty years."
questions.explanation: has/have + been + -ing = present perfect continuous.

questions.prompt: Identify the tense: "They had gone home before the storm broke."
questions.explanation: had + past participle = past perfect.

questions.prompt: Identify the tense: "By evening, I shall have written the report."
questions.explanation: shall/will + have + past participle = future perfect.

questions.prompt: Identify the tense: "He was reading a novel when I called him."
questions.explanation: was/were + -ing = past continuous.

questions.prompt: Identify the tense: "They will have been working here for ten years by June."
questions.explanation: will/shall + have been + -ing = future perfect continuous.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "My mother ___ a cake in the kitchen now."
questions.explanation: 'Now' signals an action in progress → present continuous.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "The earth ___ round the sun."
questions.explanation: A permanent truth is expressed in the simple present.
questions.trick: Universal truth → simple present.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "He ___ for two hours when the bus finally arrived."
questions.explanation: An action continuing over a period up to a past moment takes the past perfect continuous.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "I ___ this film three times so far."
questions.explanation: 'So far' (up to now) signals the present perfect.
questions.trick: so far / yet / already / ever / just → present perfect.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "The postman ___ yet."
questions.explanation: In standard British usage, 'yet' in negatives is used with the present perfect.
questions.trick: so far / yet / already / ever / just → present perfect.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "According to the timetable, the train ___ at 7 a.m. tomorrow."
questions.explanation: The simple present is used for future events fixed by a timetable or schedule.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "As soon as she ___ home, she will call you."
questions.explanation: In time clauses (when, as soon as, before, after, until) referring to the future, the simple present is used, not 'will'.
questions.trick: No 'will' after when / as soon as / until / before / if.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "It is high time we ___ home."
questions.explanation: 'It is high time' is followed by a past-tense verb, although the meaning is present.
questions.trick: It is (high) time + subject + past tense.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "I wish I ___ a bird."
questions.explanation: An unreal wish about the present uses the past subjunctive 'were' for all persons.
questions.trick: wish / if only / as if (unreal) → were.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "He talks as if he ___ the owner of this house."
questions.explanation: 'As if' expressing something unreal is followed by the past subjunctive 'were'.
questions.trick: wish / if only / as if (unreal) → were.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "Every morning my grandmother ___ to the temple."
questions.explanation: A habitual action with a third-person singular subject → simple present with -es: goes.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "Listen! Someone ___ at the door."
questions.explanation: 'Listen!' signals an action happening now → present continuous.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "I ___ in this school since I was six."
questions.explanation: An action that began in the past and continues now ('since I was six') takes the present perfect.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "The match ___ before we reached the stadium."
questions.explanation: The earlier of two past actions takes the past perfect.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "This time tomorrow, I ___ to Ooty."
questions.explanation: An action that will be in progress at a particular future moment → future continuous.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "She ___ English for five years before she moved to London."
questions.explanation: An action completed before another past action (moved) takes the past perfect.

questions.prompt: Change into indirect speech: Ravi said, "I am busy today."
options: Ravi said that he is busy today.
Ravi said that he was busy today.
Ravi said that he was busy that day.
Ravi said that I was busy that day.
questions.explanation: am → was, I → he, today → that day.
questions.trick: Past reporting verb → shift tenses one step back (am → was, has → had, will → would, can → could) and change pronouns and time words.

questions.prompt: Change into indirect speech: She said to me, "You are late."

She told me that you were late.
She said to me that I am late.
She told me that I am late.
questions.explanation: 'said to' → 'told'; 'you' (the listener, me) → I; are → was.
questions.trick: Past reporting verb → shift tenses one step back (am → was, has → had, will → would, can → could) and change pronouns and time words.

questions.prompt: Change into indirect speech: The teacher said, "The sun rises in the east."
options: The teacher said that the sun rose in the east.
The teacher said that the sun had risen in the east.
The teacher said that the sun would rise in the east.
The teacher said that the sun rises in the east.
questions.explanation: A universal truth keeps its present tense in indirect speech even after a past reporting verb.
questions.trick: Universal truths and habitual facts do NOT change tense.

questions.prompt: Change into indirect speech: He said, "I can swim across the river."
options: He said that he could swim across the river.
He said that he can swim across the river.
He said that he could swum across the river.
He said that I could swim across the river.
questions.explanation: can → could; I → he.
questions.trick: Past reporting verb → shift tenses one step back (am → was, has → had, will → would, can → could) and change pronouns and time words.

questions.prompt: Change into indirect speech: She said, "I may come late."

She said that I might come late.
questions.explanation: may → might in indirect speech after a past reporting verb.
questions.trick: Past reporting verb → shift tenses one step back (am → was, has → had, will → would, can → could) and change pronouns and time words.

questions.prompt: Change into indirect speech: Mother said, "I have cooked lunch."
options: Mother said that she has cooked lunch.
Mother said that she had cooked lunch.
Mother said that she cooked lunch.
Mother said that she was cooking lunch.
questions.explanation: Present perfect (have cooked) → past perfect (had cooked).
questions.trick: Past reporting verb → shift tenses one step back (am → was, has → had, will → would, can → could) and change pronouns and time words.

questions.prompt: Change into indirect speech: He said to me, "Where do you live?"
options: He asked me where I lived.
He asked me where did I live.
He asked me where I live?
He asked me where do you live.
questions.explanation: A wh-question becomes a statement in word order (where I lived) with 'asked'; do live → lived.
questions.trick: Reported question: question word + subject + verb, no 'do/did', full stop at the end.

questions.prompt: Change into indirect speech: The stranger said to me, "Can you show me the way to the station?"
options: The stranger asked me if I can show him the way to the station.
The stranger asked me could I show him the way to the station.
The stranger asked me whether I could show me the way to the station.
The stranger asked me if I could show him the way to the station.
questions.explanation: A yes/no question is reported with 'if/whether'; can → could; 'me' (the stranger) → him.
questions.trick: Yes/No question → asked + if/whether.

questions.prompt: Change into indirect speech: The teacher said to the students, "Do not make a noise."
options: The teacher told the students to not making a noise.
The teacher told the students not to make a noise.
The teacher said the students do not make a noise.
The teacher ordered the students that do not make a noise.
questions.explanation: A negative command is reported as 'told/ordered … not to + verb'.
questions.trick: Command → told/ordered + to-infinitive; negative → not to.

questions.prompt: Change into indirect speech: The captain said to his soldiers, "Fire!"
options: The captain requested his soldiers to fire.
The captain told his soldiers that fire.
The captain ordered his soldiers to fire.
The captain ordered his soldiers that they fire.
questions.explanation: A command is reported with 'ordered/commanded + object + to-infinitive'.

questions.prompt: Change into indirect speech: She said, "What a beautiful sunset!"
options: She exclaimed what a beautiful sunset it is.
She exclaimed that it was a very beautiful sunset.
She said what a beautiful sunset.
She asked that it was a beautiful sunset.
questions.explanation: An exclamation is reported with 'exclaimed that' and changed into a statement (What a … → very …).
questions.trick: What/How exclamation → exclaimed that … very …

questions.prompt: Change into indirect speech: He said, "Alas! I have lost my purse."
options: He exclaimed with joy that he had lost his purse.
He said alas that he has lost his purse.
He exclaimed with sorrow that I had lost my purse.
He exclaimed with sorrow that he had lost his purse.
questions.explanation: 'Alas' shows sorrow → 'exclaimed with sorrow'; have lost → had lost; I → he.
questions.trick: Alas → with sorrow; Hurrah/Bravo → with joy/applauded.

questions.prompt: Change into indirect speech: The boys said, "Hurrah! We have won the match."
options: The boys exclaimed with sorrow that they had won the match.
The boys exclaimed with joy that we had won the match.
The boys exclaimed with joy that they had won the match.
The boys exclaimed with joy that they have won the match.
questions.explanation: 'Hurrah' shows joy; we → they; have won → had won.

questions.prompt: Change into indirect speech: The old woman said to me, "May God bless you!"
options: The old woman prayed that God might bless me.
The old woman ordered God to bless me.
The old woman prayed that God may blessed me.
The old woman said that may God bless you.
questions.explanation: A wish or prayer with 'May' is reported with 'prayed/wished that … might'.
questions.trick: May (wish) → prayed/wished that … might.

questions.prompt: Change into indirect speech: He said to Sita, "I will help you tomorrow."
options: He told Sita that he will help her tomorrow.
He told Sita that he would help you the next day.
He told Sita that he would help her the next day.
He told Sita that he would help her yesterday.
questions.explanation: will → would; you → her (Sita); tomorrow → the next day.
questions.trick: Past reporting verb → shift tenses one step back (am → was, has → had, will → would, can → could) and change pronouns and time words.

questions.prompt: Change into indirect speech: She said, "I bought this book yesterday."

She said that she had bought that book the previous day.
She said that she has bought that book the previous day.
She said that she was buying that book the previous day.
questions.explanation: Simple past → past perfect; this → that; yesterday → the previous day.
questions.trick: this → that, here → there, yesterday → the previous day, ago → before.

questions.prompt: Change into indirect speech: He said, "I am living here."
options: He said that he was living here.
He said that he is living there.
He said that he had lived here.
He said that he was living there.

questions.prompt: Change into indirect speech: The boy said to the teacher, "Let me go home."

The boy ordered the teacher that he must go home.

questions.trick: Let us → suggested/proposed that we/they should; Let me/him → requested … might be allowed to.

questions.prompt: Change into indirect speech: She said to me, "Are you happy?"
options: She asked me if was I happy.
She asked me if I am happy.
She asked me if I was happy.
She asked me that I was happy.
questions.explanation: A yes/no question is reported with 'asked … if/whether' in statement order; are → was.

questions.prompt: Change into direct speech: "He told me that he was going to the market."
options: He said to me, "He is going to the market."
He said to me, "I am going to the market."
He said to me, "I will go to the market."
He said to me, "You are going to the market."
questions.explanation: Reverse the shift: was going → am going; he (the speaker) → I; told → said to.

questions.explanation: Words of nearness change to words of distance: this → that, these → those, here → there.

questions.explanation: 'Two days ago' becomes 'two days before'.
